Aiya, let me think about this year...

I've been on this land thirty years now. Twenty mu and a bit — same piece I got when we split the land. My man works construction in Handan most of the year, my son too, they come back at busy times like planting and harvest. My daughter-in-law helps some when she can. So the day-to-day, the spraying, the irrigation, the watching — that's mostly me.

We do wheat and maize, one after the other, like everyone here. No other way really, the land can't sit empty. Wheat goes in around October after the maize comes off, and the maize goes in right after wheat comes off in June. The window between is tight, maybe five, six days. No time to be slow.

**Wheat (already planted last October, harvest coming in June)**
I put in wheat in early October, around National Day time I started. Bought seed from the shop in the village — I asked old Zhao's wife what she was planting, she said Jimai 22 was doing alright the last two years, so I got that. About 12-13 kg per mu, a bit heavy because I always worry about the stand coming up thin if there's cold wind.

Before planting I spread compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, about one bag for every mu — that's 40 kg. Then the custom tractor fellow comes through, plows and drills in one pass, I pay him by the mu. Good work, faster than the old days.

Winter irrigation I did once, in early December before the ground froze, to water the roots in. Then nothing until spring. When jointing came — the stem getting thick, you can feel the node — I put urea on top, about half a bag per mu, maybe 20 kg. Then watered it in. That'll be the main growth push.

Spray — I did weeds once in early spring, the 2,4-D kind, cheap stuff. If aphids come heavy near grain-fill I'll spray once for that, but only if I see them on the heads. Last year wasn't bad, some years it's terrible.

Still need one more irrigation when the grain is filling, if the sky doesn't give rain. That's probably mid-May. Then harvest in early-mid June, I hire the combine, 50 yuan a mu.

Last year I got around 400 kg per mu on wheat. This year looks okay so far, no bad cold snap, so I'm expecting similar. Maybe 420 if the rain comes right.

**Maize (planting right after wheat harvest, around June 15-20)**
After the wheat combine leaves I hire the no-till planter — my neighbor's son has one, charges 40 yuan per mu, drops seed and a bit of starter fertilizer at once. Very fast, very good, you can't beat it on time.

For seed I usually get Zhengdan 958 or whatever that shop has that year that people say is good. Hybrid seed, about 60 yuan per mu worth. I don't save seed on hybrid, everyone knows that doesn't work.

Fertilizer — another bag of compound at planting (the planter puts it down), then when the maize is about waist-high, big whorl stage, I topdress urea, maybe 25 kg per mu. By hand, broadcast it, then watch for rain or irrigate.

Summer rain usually does a lot of the watering for maize. But if July is dry I'll irrigate once, maybe twice. The well electric is expensive, my son has to come help set up the pump. So I don't like to irrigate maize if I can avoid it.

Weeds I spray once — atrazine type, cheap. Borer I usually don't spray, too much trouble, my eyes can't handle the sprayer for long now. If the neighbors all spray I might, but usually I don't.

Harvest end of September, beginning of October. Hire the combine again, 70 yuan a mu. Then turn around and start wheat.

Expecting maize around 450 kg per mu. Last year was a good maize year, got near 500. I don't count on that every time.

**Money**
All in, I'm spending maybe 8,000 yuan on wheat inputs and 8,000 on maize, between the two seasons. Custom work is the biggest piece after fertilizer. I could save some if I did more by hand but I'm 52, not 32, and my son isn't around enough to help with the heavy work. Better to pay the machine.
